correctness.rationale: The complete proof derives the tree curvature identity from exact tree Wasserstein cut flows, obtains the universal curvature-sum feasibility limit, and uses arbitrary normalized weights and summed leaf inequalities to give a one-variable monotone lower bound. The root solves in two exact branches; an explicit feasible weighting attains it; equality in the lower bound forces the asserted unique normalized weights. Algebra proves that the activation threshold is interior iff a<b and differentiating both branch equations proves a positive jump. Finite independent checks cover 726 scalar/curvature cases, 180 constrained numerical optimizations, 300 rational endpoint cases and 180 direct Wasserstein LP edge comparisons. No finite calculation is used to infer an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The exact two-parameter prescribed-curvature profile is a natural first nontrivial bridge between the known zero-target double-star invariant and the constant-curvature terminal weight. Its asymmetric phase boundary identifies precisely when heavier-class pendant weights leave the lower bound and yields a strict interior nondifferentiability phenomenon not implied by prior general continuity or the known endpoints. The arbitrary-weight lower bound certifies that the structure survives outside symmetric ansatzes. The claim is a complete natural classification rather than an arbitrary small parameter slice; it does not purport to re-prove the already known global finite-tree existence theorem.
